thread:
tasha: Heads-up: overnight egress hardening caused a warm-pool batch in us-west-2 to hang at 0/60. Nodes repeatedly failed keystore handshakes; warm-pool remained empty for ~40m.

ben: ugh. paste the error lines?

tasha: logs: 
```
2026-04-02T01:18:04Z gpu-warm-21 keystore: decrypt err=KMS_DECRYPT_TIMEOUT attempt=5
2026-04-02T01:18:06Z gpu-warm-21 http: POST https://audit-shipper.internal/v1/logs -> 403 Forbidden
```

irene: 403 to audit-shipper means the worker egress wasn't on the new allowlist. Controlplane IPs were added, but the warm-pool uses ephemeral NAT ENIs so the rule missed them.

policy-bot: mitigation options: (A) full rollback of deny, (B) subnet CIDR allow (broad), (C) discover current NAT ENIs and add targeted allowlist entries (narrow).

ben: prefer C. We'll run a small lambda to enumerate NAT ENIs for the warm subnet and apply an allow for kms + audit endpoints for 2h. Avoids wide rollback.

tasha: agree. Also add an alert: kms.decrypt.5xx_rate > 1% for 5m and track keystore.decrypt.latency.

keystore-bot: action:apply-allowlist --subnet subnet-warm-usw2 --endpoints kms.us-west-2.internal,audit-shipper.internal --scope ENI --ttl 2h :white_check_mark:

ben: canary: launching 5 test nodes in warm-pool. watching warm_pool.fill_time and keystore.decrypt.success_rate.

irene: watch KMS QPS spike toowe saw retry storms earlier causing throttling risk and cross-region rebalance -> added egress cost (~$1.6k).

ben: canary result: 5/5 joined, decrypt.latency median 130ms (was ~2s), warm_pool.fill_time normalized, KMS 5xx rate stayed low.

tasha: next steps: 1) keep temporary allow for 2h then auto-remove, 2) open RFC to route warm-pool keystore egress through controlplane static ENI or our managed NAT, 3) add firewall CI test simulating ENI churn so future allowlists auto-enroll.

irene: for compliance: record exception (approver infra-oncall), TTL, and reason in audit logs for 180d. Security wants postmortem with root cause and remediation timeline.

tasha: I'll draft the postmortem and RFC. Closing the mitigation after TTL expiry if metrics remain healthy. :thumbsup:
